items: STORE concluded Q2 2026 with 3,590 individual property investments and $17.6 billion in AUM
The company’s portfolio demonstrates strong fund-level metrics as of Q2 2026, including a 14.8-year WALT and 2.1% weighted average annual rent bumps
Owing to its strong portfolio composition, STORE generated Q2 2026 revenues of $351 million and net income of $101 million

Substantially all of STORE Capital’s leases with tenants are structured as triple-net – insulating STORE Capital from deteriorating economics due to inflationary pressures on insurance, R&M or payroll at the property level
STORE Capital maintains its investment grade credit ratings of BBB (stable outlook) / Baa2 (stable outlook) / BBB (stable outlook) from S&P, Moody’s, and Fitch

Intel Corporation once again exceeded quarterly expectations across revenue, gross margin, and EPS, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of beating financial guidance amid strong demand and disciplined execution to expand available supply

In Q1 2026, Intel reported revenue of $13.6 billion and delivered non-GAAP EPS of $0.29, while non- GAAP net income attributable to Intel rose 156.0% YoY to $1.5 billion. The company initiated strong Q2 guidance and signaled a stronger full-year trajectory

The company's Data Center and AI segment continues to be a standout performer, generating $5.1 billion in revenue during the quarter—a 22.0% increase YoY—underscoring Intel's expanding role in AI- driven infrastructure

The Company announced new strategic initiatives during the quarter to build on the Company’s strength serving hyperscalers and other data center users. Notably, the Company announced a multi-year collaboration with Google for continued deployment of Intel’s Xeon processors and for the co- development of custom ASIC infrastructure processing units

During Q2 2026, Arko reported revenue of $2.35 billion (up ~17.4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $72.0 million (down 6.4% YoY from $76.9 million), as higher same-store operating expenses more than offset incremental benefits from the dealerization program; first-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA increased 14.0% YoY to $122.9 million

Q2 2026 retail same-store fuel margin increased to 48.7 cents per gallon (up from 45.7 cents per gallon in Q2 2025), while merchandise margin expanded 110 basis points to 34.7%; same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes declined 0.9% and same-store fuel gallons declined 5.7% amid a pressured consumer backdrop and elevated gasoline prices
Arko converted 21 retail stores to dealer locations during Q2 2026, bringing total conversions since program inception in 2024 to 471 sites
ARKO announced an agreement to acquire U.S. Petroleum Partners (USPP), expected to add ~280 million gallons of annual fuel volume and ~$30 million of annualized adjusted EBITDA
Arko maintains total liquidity of ~$1.0 billion, including $246 million in cash on hand. Net leverage stood at 2.2x

Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance reaffirmed at $245 million to $265 million, with an increased outlook for average retail fuel margin of 45.5–47.5 cents per gallon (higher margins expected to offset lower retail fuel volumes)

items: On February 24, 2025, SanDisk successfully completed its separation from Western Digital, becoming an independent public company and trading on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ‘SNDK.’ The separation of the businesses will allow the company to capitalize on unique growth opportunities within the NAND industry and operate more efficiently with a distinct capital structure
David Goeckeler assumed the role of Chief Executive Officer of SanDisk after previously serving in the same role at Western Digital

For Q4 2026, the company generated total revenues of $9.0 billion, up 51% sequentially and 372% year- over-year, with Non-GAAP operating income of $7.1 billion. Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue reached $20.2 billion, up 175% year-over-year, driven by a mix shift toward higher-value datacenter customers and higher pricing. Looking ahead, management guided Q1 FY2027 revenue of $10.3 - $10.8 billion reflecting continued benefits from AI-driven data center build-outs and sustained NAND supply tightness.

In May 2026, S&P upgraded SanDisk to BB+ from BB, citing the company's repayment of all debt and shift to a net cash position; the positive outlook reflects potential for further upgrade if business conditions remain favorable. Fitch similarly upgraded SanDisk to BB+ in April 2026.

SanDisk maintained a zero-debt balance sheet as of July 3, 2026, having repaid $1.9 billion in total debt during fiscal year 2026. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $4.8 billion, and full-year free cash flow totaled $11.5 billion.

In Q2 2026, Atlantic Union delivered strong profitability with net interest income of $325.1 million, net interest income (FTE) of $329.7 million, and net interest margin (FTE) expanding 9 basis points to 3.94%.
Return on average assets was 1.73%, return on average tangible common equity was 23.42%, and the efficiency ratio improved to 47.94%

Balance sheet quality remained a highlight with annualized net charge-offs of just 3 basis points in Q2 2026 (down from Q1's already low level), non-performing assets declining to 0.39% of loans, and criticized/classified assets easing to 4.4% of total loans. Capital levels remained robust with CET1 at 10.42%
Funding mix continued to improve, with total deposits of $30.5 billion and the loan-to-deposit ratio at 94.1% within the company's preferred 90%–95% range. Cost of funds was unchanged at 1.94%

With the Sandy Spring operational conversion now complete, Atlantic Union is pivoting to organic growth across the expanded Mid-Atlantic footprint. Record loan production in Q2 exceeded the traditionally strongest Q4 2025 by approximately 8%, with period-end loans up 10.4% annualized; management raised full-year loan growth guidance to the higher end of mid-single digits
The company is also executing its North Carolina "densification strategy," with the first Raleigh branch opening in July 2026 and a goal of 10 new branches (7 Raleigh, 3 Wilmington) by 2027

In Q1 2026, Syngenta reported $6.4 billion in revenue and $1.4 billion in EBITDA, reflecting a 5% increase year-over-year. EBITDA margin improved by ~0.6% to 21.9% driven by a higher-margin business portfolio focus, disciplined cost management, and continued operational efficiency gains
Crop protection sales were $3.5 billion, up 3% year over year. Regional performance included 18% growth in Europe, driven by biologicals, and nearly 350 product approvals in Q1 2026

The company continues to invest in R&D, with Syngenta stating continued investment in innovation and operational efficiency initiatives aimed at improving EBITDA margins and controlling capital expenditures
The company maintains investment grade credit ratings from all three major ratings agencies – Baa3 per Moody’s and BBB per S&P and Fitch

Net interest margin was 3.74% for Q2 2026; return on average assets (ROAA) was 1.09% and return on average equity (ROAE) was 10.90% for the quarter.

The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.27 per share, representing a $0.01 increase and marking the Company's 110th consecutive quarterly cash dividend. Management signaled confidence in second-half momentum, citing a significantly elevated loan pipeline and expectations for net loan growth
Gallup reported YTD June 2026 revenue of $160 million, a 0.8% decline YoY, but an EBITDA increase of 21% ($26.3 million vs $21.8 million) on lower overall production costs and SG&A discipline.
Gallup's balance sheet shows $40.3 million in cash / investments with strong FCF production (CFOA less CapEx) of $22 million.
Strategic cost management continued with a 3% reduction in business development and marketing expenses, a 14% decline in pooled costs, and a 6.5% reduction in total production costs

For Q2 2026, CommonSpirit reported normalized operating revenues of $10.3 billion, reflecting a $403 million, or 4.0%, increase over the prior year period, driven by strong volume growth and higher provider fee revenue across its network
Normalized EBITDA for the quarter reached $470 million compared to $682 million in the same period of the prior year, with normalized EBITDA margin decreasing to 4.5% from 6.7% YoY

CommonSpirit's volume trajectory remained robust, with adjusted admissions increasing 3.8% year-over- year, led by particularly strong growth in the Central region (22.4%), Mountain region (12.9%), and Northwest region (8.3%), while labor productivity continued to improve as salaries and benefits per adjusted admission declined 1.2% and FTEs per adjusted admission decreased 0.2%
CommonSpirit maintains healthy liquidity with approximately $2.7 billion of cash on hand and $17.7 billion of unrestricted cash and investments

Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA reached $1.017 billion (+8.5%), with adjusted diluted EPS of $2.21 (+18.2%).
Full-year 2026 guidance remains: net sales growth of 4%–6%, adjusted EBITDA growth of 9%–13%, and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 18%–24%

Independent restaurant case volume accelerated to +5.1% YoY - the strongest since Q4 2023 and the 21st consecutive quarter of market share gains - with healthcare volumes up 3.5% and hospitality up 4.4%. Total case volume grew 1.9%. The Pronto small-truck delivery service continued to scale, with management raising the 2027 sales target to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion

The company generated over $50 million in cost-of-goods savings in the first half through strategic vendor management and inventory optimization, with indirect spend initiatives projected to deliver over $75 million in benefits for 2026 and over $100 million by 2027

Net leverage stood at 2.6x at the end of the quarter, down slightly from FY2025 and within the company's target range of 2.0x–3.0x. US Foods' corporate credit rating remains at BB+ from S&P and Ba1 from Moody's, with the company maintaining its investment-grade BBB- secured rating

The company is embedding AI across the enterprise — including Visit Assistant for seller insights and Descartes for routing optimization — and plans to expand autonomous inventory scanning robotics to 6 additional locations by year-end

items: Sysco delivered Q4 FY2026 revenues of $22.1 billion, up 4.7% YoY, with U.S. Foodservice volume up 2.5% and U.S. local volume up 2.6%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 4.7% to $1.3 billion. The company issued FY2027 guidance of 6%–7% sales growth and 9%–11% adjusted EPS growth, supported by ~$100 million in AI-driven cost savings

The pending ~$29.1 billion acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot remains on track, expected to close by Q3 FY2027, subject to regulatory review and customary closing conditions. The transaction adds a higher-margin cash-and-carry platform with 166+ warehouse stores across 35 states and 725,000+ independent foodservice customers, creating a multi-channel distribution platform

Gross profit grew 3.7% YoY to $4.1 billion in Q4, with gross margin of 18.7% (down 17 bps YoY). For the full year, gross profit grew 4.5% to $15.6 billion with gross margin expanding 10 basis points to 18.5%, driven by positive volumes, Sysco Brand penetration gains, strategic sourcing efficiencies, and effective product cost management

Sysco holds investment-grade credit ratings of BBB / Baa2 / BBB from S&P / Moody's / Fitch. The company ended Q4 with a net debt to adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio of 2.7x, but estimated leverage pro forma for the Jetro acquisition stands at 4.5x
On March 5, 2025, Walgreens Boots Alliance announced an agreement with Sycamore Partners that would take the company private at an enterprise value of up to $23.7 billion

Based on public reporting, we believe that Sycamore’s investment strategy is aligned with the turnaround strategy enacted by existing management – this strategy refocuses Walgreens around the US Retail Pharmacy Segment (i.e., Blue Owl’s tenant)
The take-private closed in August 2025 in line with expected business plan
The Company remains compliant with all leases and based on conversations with Walgreens Real Estate leadership – Blue Owl’s portfolio is well positioned for the future

While Walgreens remains a credit that we monitor closely, we believe the completion of the take-private transaction and management's continued focus on the core pharmacy business support the long-term outlook for our leased portfolio.

On April 1, 2026, Fulton completed the acquisition of Blue Foundry Bancorp, which contributed approximately $17.5 million to Q2 net interest income; the operational integration of Blue Foundry Bank into Fulton Bank was completed on July 11, 2026

Capital ratios strengthened further as of June 30, 2026, with CET1 increasing to 12.1% (from 11.9% in Q1), Tier 1 risk-based at 12.8% (from 12.7%), total risk-based capital at 15.9% (from 15.2%), and tangible common equity ratio at 8.8%. The company also issued $300 million of 5.950% subordinated notes due 2036 and redeemed $195 million of higher-cost 3.250% subordinated notes

Non-interest income remained a meaningful contributor, increasing $9.5 million sequentially to $79.3 million, supported by record wealth management assets under management and administration of $18.4 billion (up $1.3 billion from Q1) and diversified commercial and consumer fee income streams

Fulton Bank continues to make significant technological investments including new commercial origination, mortgage origination, mortgage loan servicing, consumer origination, and customer relationship management systems to drive growth while increasing efficiency. The successful Blue Foundry integration expands Fulton's presence into Northern New Jersey, mirroring the growth strategy previously executed in Philadelphia.

Dollar General generated net sales of $10.8 billion during Q1 FY2026, a 3.4% YoY increase compared to $10.4 billion in Q1 FY2025, driven by new store openings and same-store sales growth. Operating profit increased 10.8% to $638.5 million. The company raised its full-year FY2026 diluted EPS guidance to $7.20–$7.45, while reiterating net sales growth of 3.7%–4.2%

Same-store sales increased 2.0% during the quarter, reflecting a 1.4% increase in customer traffic and a 0.5% increase in average transaction amount. Same-store sales growth included positive contributions in each of the consumables, seasonal, apparel, and home products categories
Credit metrics have continued to improve since the company's downgrade to Baa3 in March 2025. S&P affirmed Dollar General at BBB with a stable outlook

Dollar General opened 195 new stores during Q1 (190 in the U.S. and 5 in Mexico), ending the quarter with 21,055 locations. The company reiterated plans to execute approximately 4,730 real estate projects in FY2026 supported by $1.4–$1.5 billion in projected capital expenditures

items: Starbucks generated $9.3 billion of consolidated net revenue during Q3 FY2026, down 1% YoY as the China JV transition removed significant company-operated store revenue from the consolidated top line. Excluding the structural China impact, the "Back to Starbucks" turnaround continued to deliver. Non- GAAP operating margin expanded 430 basis points YoY to 14.4%, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.85. Management raised FY2026 guidance to non-GAAP EPS of $2.55–$2.65 and full-year U.S. comp growth of slightly greater than 6.0%

Global comparable store sales increased 7.9% during the quarter, primarily driven by a 4.2% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket. North America comparable store sales accelerated to 8.1%. North America segment revenue rose 7% to $7.4 billion with operating margin expanding 30 basis points to 13.6%

International segment comparable store sales increased 5.7%, driven by a 3.1% increase in average ticket and a 2.6% increase in comparable transactions. International segment reported revenue declined 34% to $1.3 billion, reflecting the conversion of China retail operations to the licensed JV model during Q3; however, international operating margin expanded 550 basis points to 19.1% as the shift to a licensed model improved the segment's margin profile
International segment revenue advanced 10% YoY, while international operating margin expanded to 19.4%

The Starbucks-Boyu Capital China JV was finalized on April 2, 2026, converting China operations from company-operated to a licensed model. Proceeds continue to be deployed toward debt reduction consistent with the company's credit profile. During Q3, Starbucks also commenced cash tender offers

Oracle reported remaining performance obligations (RPO) of $638 billion as of the fiscal quarter ended May 31, 2026 — up 363% YoY and up $85 billion sequentially from Q3. Most of the RPO increase in both Q3 and Q4 was driven by large-scale AI contracts where customers prepaid for GPU purchases or supplied their own GPUs to Oracle

The growth in Oracle's backlog has translated into robust revenue growth. The company reported $19.2 billion in revenues over the quarter ended May 31, 2026, representing YoY growth of 21% (20% in constant currency), with total cloud revenues of $9.9 billion up 47% YoY, led by Cloud Infrastructure (IaaS) revenue of $5.8 billion growing 93% YoY.

Profitability has remained strong: Adjusted EBITDA grew 26.5% year over year to $36.5Bn. EBITDA margins also expanded vs. prior year (+391bps) despite the significant upfront investment required for their AI buildout. Non-GAAP EPS climbed to $2.11, up 24% YoY. For FY2027, Oracle reaffirmed revenue guidance of $90 billion and raised Non-GAAP EPS guidance to $8.05
Despite raising nearly $37Bn in debt during the fiscal year, Net Leverage on both a balance sheet and lease adjusted basis was essentially flat to prior year at 2.7x and 3.3x respectively.

On April 16, 2026, Oracle announced an expanded multicloud partnership with Amazon Web Services. OCI now spans 26 interconnected partner cloud regions, and Oracle's Multicloud AI Database grew 404% YoY in Q4 — the fastest-growing business in company history

On July 9, 2026, S&P downgraded Oracle Corp. from BBB/Negative to BBB-/Stable citing the rapidly expanding AI Infrastructure business increasing the overall credit risk and expected continued weaker operating cash flow due to significant investments to support growth

Despite these near-term credit pressures, we remain constructive on Oracle’s credit profile given its investment-grade commitment, significant contracted backlog, strong demand for its cloud infrastructure, and balanced financing strategy; the Fund’s exposure is further supported by long-term contractual cash flows and asset-level structural protections

SouthState Bank remains the fifth largest bank in the southern United States and maintains an investment-grade issuer rating of Baa3 from Moody's and a strong A- rating from the Kroll Bond Rating Agency

Alphabet operates at exceptional scale, generating $119.8 billion of revenue in Q2 2026 (+24% YoY), marking its 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Consolidated operating income increased 30% to $40.8 billion, with operating margin expanding 2 percentage points to 34%

Alphabet's proprietary TPU infrastructure continues to drive strong demand, with Google Cloud backlog growing to $514 billion. Alphabet raised full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–$205 billion (from $180–$190 billion), with Q2 capex of $44.9 billion (+100% YoY), reflecting aggressive AI infrastructure buildout. ReSRG Automotive is a newly formed, Tier 1 auto-manufacturing company serving investment-grade, blue-chip auto OEMs including Mercedes-Benz, Toyota, Volkswagen, GM and BMW

The company was founded upon the merger of REHAU Automotive and SRG Global, two companies that were merged under the management of Atlas Holdings, a financial sponsor with more than $16 billion in AUM and deep experience in the automotive manufacturing segment

In April 2026, ReSRG Automotive expanded its strategic partnership with Valeo, a world leader in automotive lighting systems, broadening the scope of collaboration from illuminated front panels to a full range of plastic-based illuminated exterior components while simultaneously extending the geographic reach of the alliance to include China alongside the existing Europe and North America footprint

At the end of March, the company had $161mm of cash on the balance sheet, demonstrating strong liquidity
